g.text: — An Island Nation in East Asia —
Japan is an island country in East Asia, located in the northwest Pacific Ocean. It comprises four major islands — Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu — along with over 6,800 smaller islands.

With a rich cultural heritage spanning millennia, Japan seamlessly blends ancient traditions with cutting-edge modernity. From serene temples and tea ceremonies to neon-lit cityscapes and 첨단 technology, the country offers a unique contrast.

Japan's population of approximately 123 million (2024) is predominantly ethnically Japanese, with a growing foreign resident community. The capital, Tokyo, is the world's most populous metropolitan area.
Figure: Approximate locations of major cities shown on stylized map.

Japan, officially the State of Japan, is a sovereign nation with a fascinating history that spans from the ancient Jōmon period to its emergence as a modern economic powerhouse. Known for its distinctive blend of traditional arts — such as kabuki theater, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and the tea ceremony — and technological innovation, Japan has become one of the world's most influential nations. The country boasts 25 UNESCO World Heritage sites, including the historic monuments of Ancient Kyoto, the Hiroshima Peace Memorial, and the Itsukushima Shrine on Miyajima Island.

Japan's economy, once the world's second-largest, remains the fourth-largest by nominal GDP. The nation faces demographic challenges including an aging population and low birth rate, yet maintains its position as a global leader in automotive, electronics, and robotics industries. Tourism has flourished in recent years, with millions of visitors drawn to iconic destinations like Tokyo's Shibuya Crossing, the bamboo groves of Arashiyama, the floating torii gate of Itsukushima, and the majestic Mount Fuji.

Japan's nominal GDP has fluctuated significantly over the past decade. After reaching ¥5.12 trillion in 2019, the economy faced headwinds from the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent global economic shifts.

The yen's depreciation against the US dollar in 2022–2024 has had a significant impact on Japan's nominal GDP measured in current US dollars, contributing to the decline from ¥5.04 trillion (2021) to ¥4.03 trillion (2024).
Despite these fluctuations, Japan remains the world's fourth-largest economy and a major player in global trade, technology, and finance.
Source: World Bank, IMF data. Values in current US$ trillions (nominal GDP).
Sources: Statistics Bureau of Japan, UN Population Division, Japan Ministry of Internal Affairs. Figures approximate (2023–2024). "Japanese" includes both ethnic Japanese and naturalized citizens.
Capital city — Shibuya, temples, neon, Sushi, Akihabara
Ancient capital — temples, shrines, geisha district, bamboo groves
Kitchen of Japan — castles, street food, Dotonbori, Universal Studios
Peace Memorial, Itsukushima Shrine, floating torii, deer island
Japan's iconic peak — onsens, views, Fuji Five Lakes, hiking
Northern island — ski resorts, Sapporo Snow Festival, nature, seafood
✈ With 25 UNESCO World Heritage sites and diverse natural landscapes, Japan offers something for every traveler.
Sources & Notes: World Bank, IMF WEO Database, Statistics Bureau of Japan, UN DESA, Japan Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.
GDP figures in current US$ trillions (nominal). Population estimates for 2023–2024. All map locations are schematic approximations for illustrative purposes.
